arn.text: Day, the speaker of the poem, and her lover Night invite each other to a festival and trade stories, promises and gifts before their parting, and she declares they will eat a farewell feast.

On their last day together they walk across the Daraja Plains seeing everything as children, and Day recalls herding sheep with Night while he remembers her sacred rites, from which she returned a warrior with a tattooed eye.
Day announces she must leave tomorrow to war, promising to return, and she tells of how Time was once stopped and the two became as One, until Night was pulled away by the western horizon.
She concludes that they must live apart, only glimpsing each other across the sky, because neither can change.
